There she goes, rocketing through the air like a bullet. It's amazing to think that just last week, this was just a dream, or rather, a nightmare.

She calls, for the last time, just as I enter the house again. Her tone is sad, but firm, leaving me no doubt as to my future. She arrived safely, at least.

I wander about the empty halls of my home, mulling over the myriad of thought roiling through my mind like an ocean in a storm. I can't focus, so I keep pacing.

A few thoughts stick, large and consequential enough to shout through the rest. She has the kids. She has a good lawyer. She'll get the house. She always was good a manipulation. I can't work, not like this, so I won't be able to afford alimony, or child support. I'll go to jail.

The blankness of her wardrobe overwhelms me, and it's a few minutes before I can plug the torrent of tears. Was I that bad a husband? I was away a lot, sure, but that was so she could have a nice life, without worry, or want. Did she think I couldn't compromise? Maybe take a few more holidays, or fewer contracts away from home? I don't understand. I can't understand. Oh God, what is she telling the kids?

I'm in the shed. I haven't been here in months. Everything is neat and tidy, tools hang on the wall within easy grasp, utensils and odds and ends lie haphazardly arranged in drawers near the bench. The empty space is deafening. I rummage around for a few minutes before I find what I'm looking for.

Standing alone in the foyer, chair in one hand, I falter. A few more tears slip through, but I don't try to stop them. I must look a mess. I place the chair down, and head towards the bathroom. I shave carefully, and quickly shower afterwards. I put on my favourite tuxedo, and comb my hair. I admire myself in the mirror. Dignified. Powerful. In control. I head back to the foyer.

There are no tears now. Loneliness presses down upon me, and I wrap myself in it like in a blanket. I grab my items, and set to work. A few minutes later, I kick out the chair, and the rope squeezes my throat. My lungs burn, but I focus on the emptiness around me. I see the space between myself and the wall bend and glaze, as my life leaves me. As my vision darkens, I smile. The pain is gone, only a sense of fulfillment remains.

Shills' first act is always discredit, detract, derail.

The key to their divide and conquer style of posting is also the key to stopping them. They never write top-level comments. To do that, they would need ideas that are self-consistent and stand on their own merit. Instead, they always piggy back on some post that runs counter to their ideas.

One big thing that could help is a revolving moderator policy. The creator of a community should remain a moderator so long as they choose, but randomly select members of the community and invite them to moderate as well. When somebody accepts, they replace one of the current moderators (but not the community founder). When somebody is dropped from moderation, they sit out the next round of invites.

Moderator good ol' boys clubs are part of what makes forming actual communities on Reddit impossible, and they're a key part of the marketing strategy in play on that site. With decent moderation, shills wouldn't operate so freely.

Standards about how to post without derailing conversation can't be enforced without consistent moderation, and without those standards, shilling is inevitable. It's practically what this kind of platform is built for. Go ahead and try to discuss anything at all on Reddit, and see if you don't get discredited, detracted from, and derailed by somebody who doesn't even make sense.
